name: text-reveal
title: Text Reveal
description: A bold multi-line sentence that starts as faint grey text and brightens word by word as the reader scrolls through a tall section, leaving a trail of highlighted words.
use: A short statement or intro paragraph should reveal itself gradually as the reader scrolls.
avoid: Fast feeds or short pages; the tall scroll area adds a lot of blank space before it finishes.
a11y: Words start at very low contrast and the reveal never checks reduced-motion; screen readers still get the full text. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A left-aligned block of bold sans-serif text on black, wrapped over four lines. At any moment some words are solid white while the rest sit at a low grey, so the paragraph looks partly illuminated.
behaves: Scrolling through the taller section advances a progress value that maps each word from faint to full white in reading order. The text is held in a sticky panel while the scroll continues underneath.
customise: Pass the sentence as a plain string child; the type scale, spacing and sticky height are set in class names, and the per-word opacity fade is built in.
weight: light: Only word opacities are mapped to scroll progress; nothing loops in the background.
